subtitle: A synthetic editorial brief on night-program demand

slides.title: After six, the library changes
slides.subtitle: SYNTHETIC SCENARIO | Night-program demand in a fictional library system
slides.notes: All survey counts, segments, and planning parameters in this deck are invented for design evaluation.

slides.title: Q1 / Demand concentrates before eight
slides.caption: Two peak hours; overlap unknown.
sources: Synthetic scenario survey Q1, n=240; hourly multi-select
slides.footer: SYNTHETIC DATA • Illustration, not observed demand

slides.title: Q2 / One window, different reasons
slides.caption: Q2 total: 167 of 240 said yes to the 6–8 pm service window. This is separate from Q1 hourly selections.
sources: Synthetic scenario survey Q2, n=240; service-window yes/no by primary purpose
slides.footer: SYNTHETIC DATA • Counts reconcile to n=240

slides.title: A room to use, not a class to book
slides.label: of 240 prefer drop-in help
sources: Synthetic scenario survey Q3, n=240; mutually exclusive format preference
slides.footer: SYNTHETIC DATA • Format preference, not a booking forecast

slides.title: Design for arrival, then add instruction

left.title: Drop-in studio
bullets: Combines study, device help, and job search

slides.verdict: Anchor the night with an open studio; schedule one optional 30-minute lesson inside it.
sources: Synthetic scenario survey Q3, n=240; 42 respondents accepted either format
slides.footer: SYNTHETIC DATA • Preference does not measure attendance

slides.title: An eight-week test, not a new permanent hour

milestones.label: W0
milestones.title: Prepare
milestones.body: Plan two 6–8 pm nights weekly; confirm staff, access, and counts.

milestones.label: W3–6
milestones.title: Adjust
milestones.body: Try one mini-lesson; retain the open room.

sources: Synthetic planning assumptions; no real operating or cost data
slides.footer: SYNTHETIC SCENARIO • Pilot design, not authorization

slides.title: Pilot the window; earn the extension
slides.body: Test a staffed 6–8 pm drop-in studio at one branch for eight weeks.
bullets: 167 respondents favored 6–8 pm service in Q2; 127 preferred drop-in format in Q3.
Branch lead confirms staffing and safety; evaluator locks baseline and attendance protocol.
Continue only if observed visits justify staff burden. Survey cannot establish cost or equity impact.
slides.summary_callout: Pilot the window; make permanent hours depend on observed use.
sources: Synthetic scenario survey and planning assumptions; no external factual claims
